en: ... absolute opposition holds.

One kind of the oppositions is the multiplicity of living beings; the living must be considered as organizations; the multiplicity of life is opposed, one part of this multiplicity (and this part is itself an infinite multiplicity, because it is living) is considered merely in relation, having its being only as union, - the other part (also an infinite multiplicity) is considered only in opposition, having its being only through the separation from that part, and so that part too is determined as having its being only through the separation from this one.
The first part is called an organization, an individual.

It is evident of itself that this life, whose manifoldness is considered only in relation, whose being is this relation, can at the same time also be considered partly as in itself different, as mere multiplicity; its relation is no longer absolutely as the separation of this related thing; partly must also be thought with the possibility of entering into relation with what it has excluded, the possibility of the loss of individuality, or of the connection with what is excluded; - likewise the manifold that is excluded from an organic whole, which has its being only in the opposition, must at the same time be posited partly not [only] as for itself, abstracted from that organization, absolutely manifold in itself, but as at the same time standing in relation within itself, - partly also in connection with the living being excluded by it.

The concept of individuality includes within itself opposition against infinite manifoldness and connection with the same; a human being is an individual life insofar as he is an other than all the elements and than the infinity of the individual lives outside him; he is only an individual life insofar as he is one with all the elements, all the infinity of the lives outside him; - he is only insofar as the all of life is divided, he the one part, all the rest the other part; he is only insofar as he is no part and nothing is separated from him.

Undivided life presupposed, fixed, we can then consider the living127) as expressions of life, as presentations of it, whose manifoldness - which, precisely because expressions are posited, is at the same time posited, and indeed posited as infinite - reflection then fixes as resting, subsisting, as fixed points, as individuals; - or a living being presupposed, and indeed ourselves as the ones observing, then the life posited outside our limited life is an infinite life of infinite manifoldness, infinite opposition, infinite relation; as multiplicity an infinite multiplicity of organizations, individuals, as unity a single organized, separated and united whole - nature.

It is a positing of life, for into life reflection has brought its concepts of relation and separation, of the single, of what subsists for itself, and of the universal, of what is connected, the former as something limited, the latter as something unlimited, and has made it into nature through positing.
zh: ……绝对的对立有效。
对立的一类是众多有生命者；有生命者必须被看作组织；生命的杂多被对立起来，这杂多的一个部分（而这个部分本身是一个无限的杂多，因为它是活的）只被放在关系里看，它的存在只是作为结合而拥有，——另一个部分（同样是一个无限的杂多）只被放在对立里看，它的存在只是通过与那个部分的分离而拥有，于是那个部分也被这样规定，即它的存在只是通过这个部分的分离而拥有。
第一个部分叫做一个组织，一个个体。

不言自明的是，这种生命，它的杂多只在关系里被看，它的存在就是这种关系，同时也可以一部分被看作自身内不同的、单纯的杂多；它的关系不再是绝对地作为这种被关联者的分离；一部分也必须带着与它所排斥的东西进入关系的可能性来想，即丧失个体性的可能性，或与所排斥的东西结合的可能性；——同样，被一个有机整体所排斥的杂多，它的存在只在对立里，也必须同时一部分不［只］被设定为自为的、从那个组织抽象出来的、自身内绝对杂多的东西，而是被设定为自身内同时处在关系里的，——一部分也被设定为与它所排斥的有生命者相结合。
个体性的概念自身内就包含对无限杂多的对立和与这杂多的结合；一个人是个体的生命，就他是不同于一切元素、也不同于他之外那些个体生命的无限性而言；他只是一个个体的生命，就他与一切元素、与他之外一切生命的无限性是一而言；——他只是，就生命的全体被分割，他是那一个部分、其余一切都是另一个部分而言；他只是，就他不是部分、没有什么从他那里分离出去而言。

把未分割的生命先行设定、固定下来，我们便可以把有生命者127)看作生命的表露、看作生命的呈现，它们的杂多——正因为表露被设定，它也就同时被设定，而且被设定为无限的——反思随后把它固定为静止的、持存的，固定为固定的点，固定为个体；——或者把一个有生命者先行设定，而且把我们这些观察者先行设定，那么被设定在我们有限生命之外的生命，就是具有无限杂多、无限对立、无限关系的无限生命；作为杂多，它是组织、个体的无限杂多，作为统一，它是一个唯一的、组织起来的、既分离又结合的整体——自然。
它是生命的一次设定，因为反思把它关于关系与分离、关于单个的自为持存者、关于普遍的联结者的概念带进了生命，把前者当作有限的东西，把后者当作无限制的东西，并通过设定把生命变成了自然。

en: Now because life as the infinity of the living, or as an infinity of shapes, is in this way as nature an infinitely finite, an unrestrictedly restricted thing, this union of the finite and the infinite and the separation of the same within it, because nature is not itself life but a life fixed by reflection, though treated most worthily, - so the life that observes nature, that thinks, still feels, or whatever one wants to call it, this contradiction, this single opposition of itself to infinite life that still remains - or reason still cognizes the one-sidedness of this positing, of this observing -, and this thinking life lifts out of the shape, out of the mortal, transient, infinitely self-opposed, self-combating, that which is living, free from what passes away, the relation without the dead and self-killing element of manifoldness, not a unity, a thought relation, but all-living, all-powerful, infinite life, and calls it God, and is no longer thinking or observing, because its object carries nothing reflected, dead in itself128) .
zh: 既然生命作为有生命者的无限性、或作为形态的无限性，以这种方式作为自然是一个无限地有限的东西、一个无限制地被限制的东西，是有限与无限的这种结合以及两者在其中的分离，既然自然不是生命本身，而是被反思——尽管得到最有尊严的对待——固定下来的生命，那么观察自然、思考自然的生命就仍然感受到，或者随你怎么称呼它，这个矛盾，这个它自身对无限生命的唯一还存留着的对立——或者说，理性仍然认识到这种设定、这种观察的片面性——，而这种思考着的生命就从形态里、从可死的、消逝的、无限地自我对立、自我争斗的东西里，把有生命的东西提出来，摆脱了消逝之物的东西，即不带杂多中死的和自我致死的东西的关系，不是一种统一、一种被思考的关系，而是全活的、全能无限的、无限的生命，并称之为上帝，于是它不再思考或观察，因为它的对象自身内不带任何被反思的、死的东西128)。

en: This elevation of the human being, not from the finite to the infinite - for these are only products of mere reflection, and as such their separation is absolute -, but from finite life to infinite life, is religion.

Infinite life one can call a spirit, in contrast to abstract multiplicity, for spirit is the living oneness of the manifold in contrast to the same as its shape, [which] makes up the manifoldness lying in the concept of life, not in contrast to the same as a dead, mere multiplicity separated from it; for then it would be the mere unity that is called law and is a merely thought, unliving thing.
Spirit is enlivening law in union with the manifold, which is then an enlivened one.

When the human being posits this enlivened manifoldness as a multitude of many at the same time and yet in connection with the enlivening thing, then these individual lives become organs, the infinite whole an infinite all of life; when he posits the infinite life as the spirit of the whole at the same time outside himself, because he himself is something limited, posits himself at the same time outside himself, the limited one, and raises himself up to the living thing, unites himself most intimately with it, then he worships God.
zh: 人的这种提升——不是从有限者提升到无限者（因为这两者只是单纯反思的产物，作为这样的产物它们的分离是绝对的），而是从有限的生命提升到无限的生命——就是宗教。
无限的生命可以叫做一个精神，与抽象的杂多相对，因为精神是杂多的活的统一，是与作为它的形态的杂多相对而言的，这形态构成生命概念中本就有的杂多，而不是与作为从它分离出去的、死的、单纯杂多的那个杂多相对而言；因为若是那样，它就只是那叫做法律的单纯统一，是一个单纯被思考的、无生命的东西。
精神是与杂多结合中的赋生的法律，这时杂多就成了被赋生的东西。
当人把这种被赋生的杂多同时设定为许多东西的集合、却又设定为与赋生者相结合，那么这些单个的生命就成了器官，无限的整体就成了生命的无限全体；当人把无限的生命作为整体的精神同时设定在自己之外——因为他自己是一个有限的东西——，把自己也同时设定在自己、即这个有限者之外，并把自己提升到有生命者那里，与它最内在地结合，那么他就是在敬拜上帝。

en: Even if the manifold is here no longer posited as such, but occurs throughout in relation to the living spirit, as enlivened, as organ, something would thereby still be excluded and thus an incompleteness and an opposition would remain, namely the dead; in other words, if the manifold is posited in relation only as organ, then the opposition itself is excluded, but life cannot be considered as union, relation alone, but must at the same time [be considered] as opposition; if I say it is the connection of opposition and relation, then this connection can itself again be isolated and it can be objected that [it] would stand opposed to non-connection; I would have to express myself thus, that life is the connection of connection and non-connection, i.e. every expression is a product of reflection, and consequently of every one, as something posited, it can be shown that with the positing of something, at the same time an other is not posited, is excluded; this being driven onward without a resting point must however be checked once and for all by not forgetting that, for example, what was called the connection of synthesis and antithesis is not something posited, intelligible, reflected, but that its sole character for reflection is that it is a being outside reflection.

In the living whole, death, opposition, the understanding is at the same time posited, namely as manifoldness that is living and as living can posit itself as a whole, whereby it is at the same time a part, i.e. for which there are dead things and which is itself dead for others.

This being-a-part of the living is sublated in religion, limited life raises itself to the infinite; and only because the finite is itself life does it carry in itself the possibility of raising itself to infinite life.

Philosophy must precisely therefore end with religion, because the former is a thinking, thus has an opposition partly of non-thinking, partly of the thinking and the thought; it has to show finitude in everything finite and through reason [to] demand the completion of the same, especially [to] recognize the deceptions through its own infinite and so [to] place the true infinite outside its own circle.

The elevation of the finite to the infinite characterizes itself precisely thereby as the elevation of finite life to infinite, as religion, that it does not posit the being of the infinite as a being through reflection, as an objective or subjective one, so that it added the limiting to the limited, recognized this again as something posited, itself as something limited, and anew sought the limiting for it and made the demand to continue this into the infinite; this activity of reason too is an elevation to the infinite, but this infinite is a ...129)
zh: 即使杂多在这里不再是作为杂多被设定，而是处处都在对活的精神的关系中出现，作为被赋生的东西、作为器官出现，这样仍然会有一个东西被排斥在外，因而会留下一处不完满和一种对立，那就是死的东西；换句话说，如果杂多只是作为器官被设定在关系里，那么对立本身就被排斥在外了，可是生命恰恰不能只被看作结合、关系，而必须同时被看作对立；如果我说它是对立与关系的联结，那么这种联结本身又可以再被孤立起来，并且有人会反驳说，［它］是与非联结相对立的；我就得这么说：生命是联结与非联结的联结，也就是说，任何表述都是反思的产物，因此对任何一个被设定的东西都可以指出，随着某个东西被设定，同时就有另一个东西没有被设定、被排斥了；然而这种没有停顿点的被推着往前，必须一劳永逸地这样刹住：不要忘记，比如那个曾被称为综合与反题的联结的东西，并不是一个被设定的、知性的、被反思的东西，而是它对反思来说唯一的特征就在于，它是反思之外的一种存在。
在活着的整体里，死、对立、知性也同时被设定，即作为杂多被设定，这杂多是活的，并且作为活的东西能够把自己设定为一个整体，由此它同时是一个部分，也就是说，对它来说有死的东西存在，而它自己也对别的东西来说是死的。
有生命者的这种部分存在在宗教里被扬弃，有限的生命把自己提升到无限者；而且正因为有限者本身就是生命，它才在自己内带着把自己提升到无限生命的可能性。
哲学恰恰因此必须与宗教一起终止，因为前者是一种思维，所以它有一种对立，一部分是非思维的对立，一部分是思维者与被思维者的对立；它必须在一切有限者中揭示出有限性，并通过理性［去］要求对有限者的补全，尤其［去］认出由它自己的无限者所造成的种种欺蒙，从而［去］把真正的无限者设定在它自己的范围之外。
有限者向无限者的提升，恰恰由此把自己刻画为有限的生命向无限的生命的提升、刻画为宗教：它不把无限者的存在设定为通过反思而来的存在、设定为一种客观的或主观的存在，以致它给有限者添上限制者，又把后者认作一个被设定的东西、本身是一个有限的东西，并重新为它寻找限制者，还提出要求说，这要一直往无限里继续下去；理性的这种活动也是一种向无限者的提升，但这个无限者是一个……129)

en: ... an objective center; for all peoples it was the morning region of the temple and for the worshippers of an invisible God only this formless thing of determinate space, only a place.

But this merely opposed, purely objective, merely spatial thing must not necessarily remain in this incompleteness of complete objectivity, it can itself, i.e. as subsisting for itself, return through the shape to its own subjectivity.

Divine feeling, the infinite felt from the finite, is first completed by reflection being added, dwelling over it; but a relation of the same to the feeling is only a cognition of it as something subjective, only a consciousness of the feeling, separated reflection over the separated feeling; the pure, spatial objectivity gives the point of union for many, and the shaped objectivity is at the same time, what it should be, through the subjectivity connected with it not an actual but only a possible objectivity, it can be thought as such, but it is not necessary, because it is not pure.

And thereby, just as above the antinomy of time, the moment and the time of life was posited as necessary, the objective antinomy with regard to the object is posited; the being infinite in the immeasurableness of space is at the same time in determinate space, about as in the:
zh: ……一个客观的中心；对一切民族来说它是圣殿的东方，而对一位不可见上帝的敬拜者来说，它只是这确定空间中无形无状的东西，只是一个位置。
但这个单纯被对立起来的东西、纯粹客观的东西、单纯空间性的东西，并不必然停留在这完全客观性的不完满里，它本身，也就是说作为自为持存的东西，能够通过形态回到自己的主体性。
神圣的感受，即从有限者那里被感受到的无限者，只有靠反思加进来、在它上面停留，才得以补全；但反思与感受的一种关系，只是把感受认作某种主观的东西，只是对感受的一种意识，是在被分离的感受之上的被分离的反思；纯粹的空间客观性为许多人给出结合点，而有形态的客观性同时是应然的东西，通过与之相结合的主体性，它不是一种现实的客观性，而只是一种可能的客观性，它可以被这样思考，但并非必然，因为它不纯粹。
于是，正如上面时间的背反、环节和生命的时间被设定为必然的，这里也就设定了就对象而言的客观背反；那在空间的不可度量中无限的本质同时又在确定的空间里，大约就像在这句诗里：

en: He whom the heaven of all heavens did not enclose, lies now in Mary's lap.
zh: 诸天之天也容纳不下的那一位，如今躺在马利亚的怀中。

en: In religious life its relation to objects, its acting as a keeping-alive or as an enlivening of them was shown, but [it was] reminded of its fate, by virtue of which it must also let what is objective stand as objective or even itself make living things into objects.
It can be that this making-objective must be only for the moment and that life again withdraws from it, frees itself from it and leaves what was suppressed to its own life and its resurrection.
But it is necessary that it also enters into a lasting relation with objects, preserves objectivity for them up to complete annihilation.

With all the increased religious union shown by the completions so far, hypocrisy can still take place, namely through particular property held back for itself; with the firm having of things the human being would not have fulfilled the - negatively expressed - conditions of religion, namely to be free of absolute objectivity, to have raised himself above finite life; he would be incapable of union with infinite life, because he would still have kept something for himself, would still be caught in a dominating or entangled in a dependence; and therefore he gives up property, whose necessity is his fate, as sacrifice, - only some of it, for his fate is necessary and cannot be sublated, he annihilates a part also before the deity, from the annihilation of the rest he takes away particularity through commonality with friends, as much as possible, and through the fact that it is a purposeless excess; and through this purposelessness of annihilation alone, through this annihilating for the sake of annihilating, he makes good his otherwise particular relation of purposive annihilation and has at the same time completed the objectivity of the objects through an annihilation not related to itself, their complete relationlessness, death, and if the necessity of a relating annihilation of the objects remains, yet this purposeless annihilating for the sake of annihilating sometimes occurs, which proves itself as the only religious one toward absolute objects.
zh: 在宗教生活里，它同对象的关系、它作为把对象保持为活或把对象赋生的行动，已经显示出来了，但也要记起它的命运：由于这命运，它也必须让客观的东西作为客观的东西存在下去，甚至自己把有生命的东西变成对象。
可能的是，这种造成对象化只须持续一瞬间，生命又重新离开它，把自己从它那里解放出来，把被压制的东西交给它自己的生命和它的复活。
但它也必然要把自己放进与对象的持久关系里，把对象性一直保持到完全的毁灭。

即便有此前那些补全所显示出的增多了的宗教结合，伪善仍然可能发生，也就是通过特别的、为自己留存下来的财产；人若牢牢占有东西，就没有满足——用否定的话说——宗教的条件，即摆脱绝对的客观性、把自己提升到有限生命之上；他就没有能力与无限的生命结合，因为他还会为自己留下点什么，还陷在一种支配里，或困在一种依赖之下；因此他把财产作为献祭交出去，财产的必然性就是他的命运，——只交出一些，因为他的命运是必然的，不能被扬弃，他也在神面前毁灭一部分，对其余部分的毁灭，他通过与朋友们的共同性尽量去掉了它的特殊性，也通过使它成为一种无目的的过剩；单凭毁灭的这种无目的性，单凭这种为毁灭而毁灭，他就补赎了他其余那种合目的地毁灭的特殊关系，同时也通过一种不与自身相关的毁灭、即对象的完全无关系、死，把对象的客观性完成了，而即便对象的一种建立关系的毁灭的必要性仍然存在，这种为毁灭而毁灭的无目的毁灭有时还是会出现，它证明自己是面对绝对对象时唯一宗教性的毁灭。

en: It need only be touched on briefly that the remaining external spatial surroundings, as a necessary limitation, must not so much occupy us by purposeless beauty itself as have to point to something else by purposive embellishment; and that it is the essence of divine service to sublate the contemplative or thinking contemplation of the objective God, or rather to fuse it with the subjectivity of the living in joy, [by means of] song, bodily movements, a kind of subjective utterance which, like sounding speech, becomes objective and beautiful through rule and can turn into dance, - a manifoldness of occupations, of the ordering of the offering, of sacrificing, etc. Also, this multiplicity of utterances and of those uttering requires unity, an order which as something living is an ordering, commanding being, a priest, who likewise becomes something set apart when a needful external life of human beings has become very separated; not to mention other consequences and their completions.
zh: 只需再简短地提一下：其余那些外在的空间环境，作为一种必要的界限，与其说可以用无目的的美本身来占用我们，不如说它要通过合目的的修饰去指向另一个东西；而礼拜的本质，就是扬弃那种对客观上帝的直观的或思维的考察，或者说，毋宁把它与活生生的主体性在欢乐中融合起来，[借助]歌唱、身体的运动、一种主观的表达方式——这种表达方式像发出声音的言说那样，通过规则而成为客观的、美的，可以变成舞蹈——以及活动的杂多、献上的安排、献祭等等。再者，这种表达和表达者的杂多也要求统一，要求秩序，而这种秩序作为活生生的东西就是一个进行安排、发出命令的存在者，即一位祭司；当人们那种充满需求的外在生活已经十分孤立时，这位祭司同样会成为一个被分离出来的东西；至于其他的后果及其补全，就不必提了。

en: This more complete union in religion, such an elevation of finite life to infinite life, that as little finite, limited, i.e. purely objective or purely subjective, remains over as possible, that every opposition that has itself arisen in this elevation and completion is again completed, is not absolutely necessary; religion is some elevation of the finite to the infinite as a posited life; and such an elevation is necessary, for the former is conditioned by the latter; but at which stage of opposition and union the determinate nature of a race of human beings comes to a stop is accidental with respect to the indeterminate nature.

The most perfect completeness is possible among peoples whose life is as little torn and divided as possible, i.e. among happy ones; more unhappy ones cannot reach that stage, but in the separation they must concern themselves with the preservation of one member of it, with self-subsistence; they must not seek to lose this, their highest pride must be to keep the separation firm and to preserve the One; one may now consider this from the side of subjectivity as self-subsistence or from the other side as a foreign, distant, unattainable object; both seem to be compatible side by side, however necessary it is that, the stronger the separation, the purer the I and at the same time the further the object is above and far from the human being; [that,] the greater and more set apart the inner, the greater and more set apart the outer and, if the latter is posited as the self-subsistent, the more subjugated the human being must appear; but precisely this being-ruled by the over-great object is what is held fast as relation; it is accidental which side his consciousness takes up, whether that of fearing a God who is infinitely exalted above all heavens of heavens, above all belonging through connection, over-powerful hovering above all nature, or [that of] positing oneself as pure I above the ruins of this body and the shining suns, above the thousand-thousand world-bodies and the so many times new solar systems, as all of you are, you shining suns.

If the separation is infinite, then the fixing of the subjective or the objective is indifferent; but the opposition remains, absolute finite against absolute infinite; the elevation of finite life to the infinite life could only be an elevation above finite life; the infinite is the most complete in so far as it is opposed to totality, i.e. to the infinity of the finite, not in so far as this opposition would be sublated in beautiful union, but in so far as the union is sublated and the opposition is a hovering of the I above all nature or the dependence on, more correctly: the relation to, a being above all nature.

This religion can be sublime and terribly sublime, but not beautifully human; and so the bliss in which the I has everything, everything opposed, under its feet is an appearance of time, in substance equivalent to that of depending on an absolutely foreign being that cannot become human, or [to the fact] that, if it had become this (thus in time), it would in this union too remain an absolutely particular, only an absolute One - the most worthy, noblest thing, if the union with time were ignoble and base.
zh: 宗教中这种更完整的结合，这种把有限生命提升到无限生命——使残留下来的有限者、受限制者，也就是纯粹客观的或纯粹主观的东西尽可能少，使每一个即使是在这种提升和补全中产生出来的对立又得到补全——并不是绝对必然的；宗教是把有限者提升到作为被设定的生命的无限者的某种提升；而这样一种提升是必然的，因为前者是由后者制约的；但一个人类族类的特定本性停留在对立和结合的哪一个阶段上，相对于那种不确定的本性来说是偶然的。

最完美的完整性在那些生命尽可能少被撕裂和分割的民族那里是可能的，也就是说，在幸福的民族那里是可能的；更不幸的民族达不到那个阶段，相反，他们在分离中不得不操心保住分离中的一个环节，操心自立；他们不可以试图失去这种自立，他们最高的骄傲必须是让分离牢固并保住那一个东西；人们现在可以从主体性这一面把它看作自立，也可以从另一面把它看成一个陌生的、遥远的、达不到的客体；两者看来可以并存相容，尽管下面这一点是必然的：分离越强，我越纯粹，同时客体就越是高居于人之上、远离人；内在越大、越被隔开，外在也就越大、越被隔开，而如果后者被设定为自立的东西，人就必然显得越受奴役；但恰恰是这种被过大的客体所支配，才是被当作关系而紧紧抓住的东西；他的意识抓住哪一面是偶然的：是去畏惧一个上帝——他无限地高居于一切诸天之上，高居于一切通过联系而来的归属之上，悬浮在一切自然之上而拥有过大的力量——还是[去]把自己作为纯粹的我置于这具身体的废墟之上、置于那些发光的太阳之上、置于千千万万的天体之上、置于那么多回重新出现的太阳系之上，就如同你们全体那样，你们这些发光的太阳。

如果分离是无限的，那么把主观的东西还是客观的东西固定下来就无所谓了；但对立依然存在：绝对的有限者对抗绝对的无限者；把有限生命提升到无限生命，只可能是一种超出有限生命的提升；无限者是最完整的东西，这是就它被与总体、即有限者的无限性对立起来而言，不是就这种对立在美的结合中被扬弃而言，而是就结合已被扬弃、对立成了我在一切自然之上的悬浮，或者成了对一个在一切自然之上的存在的依赖——更准确地说：关联——而言。
这种宗教可以是崇高的，甚至是可怕地崇高的，但不是美的、人性的；因此，那种我把一切、把一切对立的东西都踩在脚下的至福，是时间的现象，实质上等同于这样一种至福：依赖一个绝对陌生的、不能成为人的存在；或者等同于这样：即使它成了人（也就是说在时间中成了人），在这种结合中它也仍然是一个绝对特殊的东西，只是一个绝对的一——如果与时间的结合是卑下的、下贱的，那它倒是最可敬、最高贵的东西。

en: Spirit of the Orientals: respect for actuality in actuality and embellishment of it in the imagination. - The Orientals have firmly determinate characters.
As they once are, they no longer change.
The direction of the path they have entered upon they do not leave.
What lies outside their path is not present for them.
But what disturbs them on the path is hostile to them.
Their once firmly determinate character cannot let go of itself, cannot take up into itself what is opposed to it and reconcile itself with it.
The one becomes ruling, the other something ruled.
Power is the concept in which the beings are alike.
Violence their relation to one another, violence of strength or of genius or of speech.

A firmly determinate character admits nothing outside itself except what it rules or by which it is ruled just as that is ruled by it; for there are limits, actualities in it, which cannot be sublated, which, in order to subsist alongside other contradictory actualities, alongside what is hostile, can stand in no other relation.
Since the limits of the character yield actualities that love cannot unite, they must be connected objectively, i.e. stand under a law.
The same in actuality is necessity, thus the law that rules everything.
That is why in the oriental character the two apparently contradictory determinations - lust for rule over everything and willing submission to every slavery - are so intimately bound together.
Over both rules the law of necessity.
Domination and slavery, both states are just here, for in both of them the same law of violence governs.

In the Orient the happy man is the one who has the courage to subject to himself what is weaker than he, and possesses the prudence not to attack what is stronger than he but to submit to it just the same.
Here the wise man is the one who withdraws from the actualities and is active in speech and in sayings.

Noble is the more cultivated man, who knows how to distinguish and subjugates only in so far as he has been resisted, and thereby puts himself on a level with the conquered by recognizing over himself together with him the law of necessity; [who sees] in himself, the actual victor, the possible conquered, and at the same time honours in the actually subjugated the possible ruler.

This possibility of the opposed, this possibility of the infinite manifoldness of actual things as possible rulers or as possible subjugated, this power that appears in the transitions of the negative into the positive, of the positive into the negative, is the infinite divinity of the Orientals.

On the loom of their will and their government the events are woven, and out of the source of his command the streams of times and centuries flow into the abyss of his power. - With the firm determinateness of the oriental character there are very few relations in which the human being stands, and everything that presents itself soon receives its place.
The human being of firmly determinate character gets involved with nothing that is not homogeneous with him.
Most of what can strike against him he pushes aside.
The other he fights and becomes master over it, or submits to violence, but his claims remain the same.
This unchangeableness, this incapacity to be moved in many directions by the manifoldness of things, preserves for the Oriental his calm.

Because for him the world is a collection of actualities and these appear only in their naked shape as mere opposed things, without their own soul and spirit, he must, in order to remedy their poverty, necessarily seek to replace by a foreign, borrowed splendour what they lack in their own content.
The Oriental always embellishes actuality with the power of imagination.
He wraps every thing in images.
These images too are indeed images of actualities, and the one poverty seems able to impart no splendour to the other, but through their connection they become poetic.
The union of the heterogeneous produces an illusion of life that lies in the sameness of the connected.
That in which one knows them to be similar comes, because the different is so heterogeneous, to a dark consciousness, but they cannot venture to let a shape of pure life emerge.
The sublime splendour of their images astonishes, the sun-brightness of their paintings is dazzling.

But precisely because one feels the violence in the union of heterogeneous things, one is astonished; because one can lay no claim to the splendour of this objective element, one is dazzled; because love has not united them, feeling comes away empty here, and the precious things, the pearls of the oriental spirit, are only wildly beautiful monsters.

But where the objectivity of life, stripped off from the manifold, emerges as unity, there this can only be a concept, a universal, with which their paintings are filled. - The determinateness of the character allows no great manifoldness of characters.
The manifoldness of the determinations would shatter itself.
But what lies beyond these determinations, indeed homogeneous with it in substance, yet of greater and deeper force, that had to work as something invisible, higher, wonderful.

In the manner of composition of the oriental lasting or ephemeral empires, from the system of obedience and subordination in such wild masses, there clearly shows itself the power that oriental, hence homogeneous, but with strength, depth and obstinacy combined characters exercise over other Orientals, the blind, almost to annihilation going passivity of the latter towards the former.

Hence too springs the importance, and therefore the sparingness and the seriousness of speech, of the utterance of an invisible and in itself unrecognizable life. - As the Orientals embellish the naked actuality of other things with the imagination, so they, who have so incomplete a consciousness of themselves and can find no satisfying oneness in the presentation of their nature, must overload themselves so greatly with foreign ornaments.

Their ornament cannot be a clothing that would receive its form and beauty from the human figure and its own free play, but wholly foreign things; and here no natural wholes, which one rather pins on oneself out of love and in doing so adorns oneself more with one's own feeling, but shining things stripped of their own life and of a shape formed by life, gold, perhaps clothed in borrowed forms, ornaments united in flowers, etc. - Among the Orientals, precisely nature had been driven out of the natural, and for itself it appeared only as something common and subjugated.
The feminine mind and the love of women alone was no such passion whose enjoyment was domination.

Among many oriental nations it is a high dishonour, especially among the distinguished, to mention the women and what relates to them: either because here even the bravest did not feel themselves masters and were thereby reminded of their weakness; or rather, since none of them was ashamed of this weakness before himself and held only the mention, the utterance of everything that related to this side of human nature to be a dishonour, because they honoured the feminine as something foreign to their remaining spirit, as something superior to them, and were shy of placing it, by the mention, in the class of the remaining multitude of common things.

Because they feel that the relation to women can never become what the relation to all other things is, domination or servitude, and that women are for them something that cannot be treated like these and of which they can [not] become sure, they know no other counsel than to lock them up! - The Jews did not have that shyness.
They spoke of sexual relations freely and without ceremony, but everything that relates to them is for them, like everything, a merely actual thing, not permeated by the spirit of love.

This spirit therefore does not rule them in the treatment of this matter either, and this treatment is therefore, in their very laws and in the books that contain the sum of their culture, so outrageous, base and shameful; for the holier and purer the quickening being is, the more abominable it is to present and treat its organs and its utterances as mere things. - Among the Orientals the beard is very holy.
Among the Jews no razor might come upon the head of a Nazirite or of one consecrated to God.
Every seventh, perhaps also fiftieth year, which were consecrated to God, no field might be cultivated, no vine pruned, no vintage held.
Of the voluntary produce of the earth, servants, cattle and wild animals were to be able to take free part.
It is a very great arbitrariness to let the beard grow.

It is indeed an organ of the body, but in a very slight degree, and in this respect cutting the nails is just as much, and circumcision, so customary among the Orientals and commanded among the Jews, is probably an even greater mutilation.

The retention of the beard can therefore not be regarded as a respect for the completeness of the human figure, which respect, moreover, flatly contradicts the hiding of the figure by tasteless clothing and its overloading with shining and multifarious ornament.

An arbitrariness that one imposes on oneself as a law is asserted with all the greater obstinacy, just as the self-sacrifice has all the more merit the greater the arbitrariness is to which one submits.
But why did the Orientals impose precisely this arbitrariness on themselves?
Why with the importance that the beard is even something holy?

Since in the oriental spirit all value and stability is in the infinite object, since it can set no store by something that subsists for itself, that has its own life in itself, it must deck itself out from outside through shining things in which there is no life, must after all also make itself into something, and thus also seek to preserve the beard, which is the most inessential thing about its organic wholeness, most of all, to honour most of all the most indifferent thing about it.
zh: 东方人的精神：在现实性中尊重现实性，并在想象力中美化它。——东方人有固定确定的性格。
他们一旦是什么样子，就不再改变。
他们已经走上的那条路的方向，他们不会离开。
在他们道路之外的东西，对他们来说并不存在。
但他们在路上受到妨碍的东西，对他们来说就是敌意的。
他们一旦固定确定的性格不能放下自身，不能把与自己相对立的东西接纳进自身，并与之和解。
一方成为统治者，另一方成为被统治者。
权力是诸存在者在其中彼此相同的那一概念。
暴力则是他们彼此之间的关系，是力量、天才或言辞的暴力。
一个固定确定的性格，除了它所统治的东西，或者像它统治对方那样反过来被对方统治的东西之外，不容许任何东西在自身之外；因为在他身上有一些不能被扬弃的界限、现实性，这些界限为了能与其他相矛盾的现实性、与敌意的东西并存，不能处在任何别的关系之中。
由于性格的种种界限产生出爱所不能结合的现实性，所以它们必须被客观地联结起来，也就是说，处在一条法则之下。
现实性中相同的东西就是必然性，也就是统治一切的法则。
所以，在东方人的性格中，那两个看来互相矛盾的规定——对一切都要统治的贪求和对任何奴役都心甘情愿的顺服——才如此紧密地结合在一起。
在两者之上都支配着必然性的法则。
统治和奴役，这两种状态在这里都是公正的，因为在两者之中都支配着同一条暴力的法则。
在东方，幸福的人就是有勇气把比自己弱的东西制服于自己、又有精明不去攻击比自己强的东西而是同样顺从地屈服于它的人。
在这里，智者就是从种种现实性中抽身、在言辞和箴言中活动的人。
高贵的是那个更有教养的人，他懂得区分，只在他遭到抵抗的限度内才去征服，并且因此与被战胜者平起平坐，因为他承认那必然性的法则同样支配着自己和对方；他在自己这个现实的胜利者身上[看到]那个可能被战胜的人，同时又在真正被制服的人身上尊敬那个可能的统治者。
这种对立者的可能性，这种现实的东西作为可能的统治者或可能的被征服者的无限杂多的可能性，这种在否定者向肯定者、肯定者向否定者的过渡中出现的权力，就是东方人的无限的神性。
在他们的意志和他们的统治的织机上，事件被织出来；从他那命令的源头，时间和世纪的河流流进他那权力的深渊。——由于东方人性格那种固定的确定性，人所处的关系非常少，而一切呈现出来的东西很快都得到自己的位置。
具有固定确定性格的人，不与任何与他不同类的东西打交道。
大多数可能碰到他的东西，他都推到一边去。
其他的东西他就与之斗争，或者成为它的主人，或者屈服于暴力，但他的要求始终不变。
这种不变性，这种不能为事物的杂多所多方打动的无能，替东方人保住了他的平静。
因为对他来说，世界是一堆现实性的集合，而这些现实性只以赤裸的形态作为单纯对立的东西出现，没有自己的灵魂和精神，所以他为了补救它们的贫乏，就必然要设法用外来的、借来的光辉，去替代它们自身内容所缺少的东西。
东方人总是用想象力来美化现实性。
他把每样东西都裹进形象里。
这些形象虽然也是现实性的形象，而且一种贫乏看来不能给另一种贫乏增添什么光辉，但它们通过自己的联结而变得富有诗意。
不同类东西的结合产生出生命的一种假象，这种生命在于被联结双方的相同之中。
人们据以认出它们相似的那个东西，由于这些不同者如此不同类，只达到一种模糊的意识，但他们不敢让纯粹生命的一种形态呈现出来。
他们形象的崇高壮丽令人惊叹，他们图画的太阳般的光辉令人目眩。
但正因为人在不同类东西的结合中感觉到那种强暴，人才惊叹；因为人不能对客观东西的这种壮丽提出要求，人才被弄得目眩；因为爱并没有把它们结合起来，所以感受在这里空手而归，而东方精神的那些珍宝、那些珍珠，只不过是野性之美的怪物。
但是，当生命的客观性摆脱杂多的东西而作为统一出现时，这种统一就只能是一个概念、一个普遍者，他们的图画所充满的就是这个东西。——性格的确定性不允许有大量杂多的性格。
这些规定性的杂多会自己把自己打碎。
但在这些规定性之外的东西，虽然就事情本身说与它同类，却具有更大、更深的力，这种东西就必然作为某种看不见的、更高的东西奇妙地起作用。
从东方那些持久的或短暂的帝国的构成方式中，从这种野蛮的群众中的服从和从属体系里，清楚地显示出东方的、因而同类的、但结合着力量、深度和顽固的性格对另一些东方人施加的权力，以及后者对前者那种盲目的、几乎走向毁灭的被动性。
由此也产生了言辞的重要性，因而也产生了言辞的节省和严肃——言辞是一种看不见的、自在不可认识的生命的表达。——正如东方人用想象力美化其他事物的赤裸现实性，他们既然对自身只有如此不完整的意识，又不能在表现自己的本性时找到令人满足的一致，也就必然要用外来的装饰把自己堆砌得如此过分。
他们的装饰品不可能是一种从人的形象和形象自身的自由游戏中获得形式和美的衣着，而完全是陌生的东西；而且不是那种自然的整体——人们佩戴它们更多是出于爱，并且由此更多是用自己的感受来装饰自己——而是被剥夺了自身生命和由生命塑形的形态的闪亮东西，黄金，也许还被套上借来的形式，还有在花里结合起来的装饰等等。——在东方人那里，自然的东西中恰恰是自然被驱逐掉了，自然本身只显得是低贱的、被制服的东西。
女性的心灵和对女人的爱本身，并不是那样一种激情：它的享受就是统治。
在许多东方民族那里，提到女人以及和女人有关的事情是一种极大的耻辱，尤其是在贵人中间：这或者是因为，在这里连最勇敢的人也不觉得自己是主人，因而被提醒了自己的软弱；或者更确切地说，是因为没有人在自己面前为这种软弱感到羞耻，而只把提到、说出一切与人性这一面有关的东西视为耻辱，因为他们把女性当作某种与他们其余的精神格格不入、高于他们的东西来尊敬，并且生怕一提到它，就把它放到其余那些低贱东西的行列里去。
因为他们感觉到，与女人的关系永远不能成为与所有其他东西的关系的那种东西，即统治或奴役，而且女人对他们来说是某种不能像这些东西那样对待、他们也无法对之[不]放心起来的东西，所以他们想不出别的办法，只好把她们关起来！——犹太人没有那种羞怯。
他们自由地、毫不拘束地谈论两性关系，但与此相关的一切，对他们来说就像一切东西一样，只是单纯现实的东西，没有被爱的精神所渗透。
因此，这一精神在处理这个题材时也不支配他们，所以这种处理在他们的法律本身中，以及在包含他们教养之总和的书里，才如此令人愤慨、卑劣可耻；因为赋予生命的本质越神圣、越纯粹，把它的器官和它的表现当作单纯的东西来表现和处理，就越可恶。——在东方人那里，胡子是非常神圣的。
在犹太人那里，拿细耳人或献给上帝的人头上不许动剃刀。
每一个第七年，也许还有第五十年，都是献给上帝的，在那一年里不许耕种田地，不许修剪葡萄藤，不许收葡萄。
对于土地自愿出产的东西，奴仆、牲畜、野兽都应当能够自由地分享。
让胡子长起来，是一种极大的任意。
它固然是身体的一个器官，但只是在极低的程度上是，就这一点说，剪指甲同样是一种残损，而在东方人那里如此常见、在犹太人那里被规定下来的割礼，大概还是更大的残损。
所以，保留胡子不能看作是对人的形象之完整性的尊重，何况这种尊重与用毫无品味的衣着把形象遮掩起来、又用闪亮的、繁多的装饰把它堆砌得过分的做法，是绝对矛盾的。
一个人自己给自己立为法则的任意，会被越发固执地坚持，正如人们所服从的任意越大，牺牲也就越有功劳。
但东方人为什么偏偏给自己立下这种任意呢？
为什么还要带着这样的重要性，说胡子甚至是某种神圣的东西？
由于在东方精神中，一切价值和持存都在那个无限的客体里，由于它不能看重某种自为地持存、在自身中拥有自己生命的东西，所以它必须从外面靠那些其中没有生命的闪亮东西来打扮自己，毕竟也要把自己弄成点什么，因此也就最想保住胡子——胡子是它有机整体中最不本质的东西——最尊敬自己身上最无所谓的东西。

en: Memory is the gallows on which the Greek gods hang strangled.

To show a gallery of such hanged men, to drive them round in a circle with the wind of wit, to make them tease one another and to blow them into all sorts of groups and distortions, is often called poetry. - Memory is the grave, the repository of the dead.
The dead thing rests in it as something dead.
It is pointed out like a collection of stones.

Ordering, going through, dusting, all these occupations do indeed have a relation to the dead, but they are independent of it. - But to babble incomprehensible prayers, to read masses, to say rosaries, to practise devotional ceremonies empty of meaning, this is the doing of the dead.
The human being tries to become wholly an object, to let himself be governed entirely by something foreign.
This service is called devotion.
Pharisees!
zh: 记忆就是那副绞架，希腊诸神被勒死了挂在上头。
把这样一批被绞死的人陈列成一条画廊，用机智的风吹得他们团团转，让他们彼此戏弄，把他们吹成各种各样的组合和扭曲的形状，这常常就叫作诗。——记忆是坟墓，是死者的存放处。
死的东西在里面就是作为死的东西安放着。
它被指出来，就像一堆石头。
整理、翻检、掸灰，所有这些忙碌固然同死者有关系，却是独立于死者的。——可是结结巴巴地念些听不懂的祷词、做弥撒、数念珠、搞毫无意义的礼拜仪式，这才是死者的行动。
人试着完全变成客体，让自己彻底被一个异己的东西支配。
这种侍奉就叫作虔诚。
法利赛人！

en: Mourning women at the public funeral of those who fell in the first year of the Peloponnesian War.
Thucydides B, λ δ: καὶ γυναῖκες πάρεισιν αἱ προσήκουσαι ἐπὶ τὸν τάφον ὀλοφυρόμεναι.131) The greatest relief of pain is to cry it out, to have said it purely in its whole extent.
Through the utterance the pain is made objective and the equilibrium is established between the subjective, which alone is present, and the objective, which in pain is nothing.
Through the utterance alone does it come to consciousness, and what has come to consciousness is then over and done with.
It is brought into the form of reflection and is pushed away by the following determinations.
But if the mind is still full, if the pain is still wholly subjective, then nothing else has room in it.
Tears too are such a discharge, such an utterance, an objectification of pain.
The pain has then, since it is subjective and has also become objective, made itself into an image.
But since pain is by its nature subjective, it is very contrary to it to go out of itself.
Only the utmost need can drive it to that.
Even when the need is over, when everything is lost and it has become despair, it still shuts itself up in itself, and here it is most beneficial to bring it out.
Through nothing heterogeneous can this happen.
Only in that it is given to itself does it have itself as itself and as something partly outside itself.
A painting does not have this effect.
He only sees, but does not move himself.
Speech is the purest form of objectivity for the subjective.
It is not yet anything objective, but it is still the movement toward objectivity.
Lament in song has at the same time still more the form of the beautiful, because it moves according to a rule.

Laments sung by hired women are therefore the most human thing for pain, for the need to discharge oneself of it, in that one lets it develop most deeply and holds it before oneself in its whole extent.
Only this holding-before alone is the balm.
zh: 哭丧妇，在伯罗奔尼撒战争第一年阵亡者的公开葬礼上。
修昔底德 B, λ δ：καὶ γυναῖκες πάρεισιν αἱ προσήκουσαι ἐπὶ τὸν τάφον ὀλοφυρόμεναι.131) 痛苦最大的缓解，就是把它哭喊出来，把它纯然完整地说了出来。
通过说出来，痛苦被弄成了客观的，而主观之物与客观之物之间的平衡也就此建立起来：前者是唯一现成存在的东西，后者在痛苦里什么都不是。
只有通过说出来，它才进入意识，而凡进入了意识的东西，随后就已经过去了。
它被带进反思的形式，并被下面这些规定排挤开。
可是只要心情还是满的，痛苦还完全是主观的，别的东西就在里面占不到位置。
眼泪也是这样的一种宣泄，这样的一种表达，是痛苦的一种客观化。
这时候痛苦既然既是主观的、又已成为客观的，它就把自己弄成了一幅图像。
但痛苦按其本性是主观的，所以走出自身对它来说是很违背本性的。
只有极端的困厄才能逼它这么做。
即使困厄已经过去，即使一切都失去了、痛苦已经变成绝望，它仍然把自己关在自己里面，而这时候把它带出来，是再有益不过的。
这件事靠任何异质的东西都做不到。
只有把它给予它自己，它才既拥有作为它自身的自己，又拥有作为部分地在自身之外的自己。
一幅画产生不了这种效果。
他只是看，自己却并不动。
对于主观的东西来说，言语是客观性最纯粹的形式。
它还不是什么客观的东西，但已经是朝客观性去的运动。
哀哭一旦唱出来，就同时还更多地带有一层美的形式，因为它是按一定的规则进行的。
所以雇来的妇女唱的哀歌，对于痛苦、对于要把痛苦宣泄出去的需要来说，是最合乎人性的东西，因为人由此让痛苦最深地展开，并把它在全部范围里摆在自己眼前。
只有这种摆在自己眼前，本身才是那帖香膏。

en: Thukydides B, λ ς: τὰ δὲ πλείω αὐτη ͂ς (ὅσην ἔχομεν ἀρχὴν) αὐτοὶ ἡμει ͂ς οἵδε οἱ νυ ͂ν ἔτι ὄντες μάλιστα κ. τ. λ.132) So only the popular assembly of a small free state can speak.
Before it and from its mouth such "we" have complete truth.
In larger republics they are always very limited.
The "we" is always the more foreign to those who utter it, the greater the multitude of their fellow citizens is.
The share of each individual in a deed is so small that he can hardly speak of it as his deed at all.
The share in the fame of his nation is greater, but it only means: I belong to the nation, not: I am.
This whole exercises a dominion over him, under which he stands.
A free great people is therefore in this respect a contradiction in itself.
The people is the totality of all individuals, and all every[one] are always the ruled by the whole.
Their deed, that which is the deed of each one, is an infinitely small fragment of a national action.
zh: 修昔底德 B, λ ς：τὰ δὲ πλείω αὐτη ͂ς (ὅσην ἔχομεν ἀρχὴν) αὐτοὶ ἡμει ͂ς οἵδε οἱ νυ ͂ν ἔτι ὄντες μάλιστα κ. τ. λ.132) 所以只有一个小自由邦的公民大会才能这样说话。
在它面前、从它口中说出的这种“我们”，才有完全的真理。
在更大的共和国里，它们总是受到很大限制。
说“我们”的人，同胞的数量越大，“我们”对他就越是陌生。
每个人在一桩行为中所占的份额小到，他几乎根本没法把它说成自己的行为。
他在自己民族荣誉里占的份额要大一些，但那只是说：我属于这个民族，而不是说：我就是。
这个整体对他行使一种统治，他就处在这种统治之下。
所以，一个自由的大民族就此而言是自相矛盾的。
民族是所有个人的总体，而所有每一个[人]都总是被整体支配的人。
他们的行为，也就是每个人所做的行为，是一项民族行动中无限小的一块碎片。

en: Achilles died, wounded by an arrow in the heel.
He could just as well have been wounded at any other point of his body.
The wound at that part was therefore the merest accident.
By the direction of the arrow it was thoroughly determined.
But the one struck was, in regard to the remaining parts (to which he, since he makes a whole with them, must necessarily be related), distinguished as the wounded, struck part.

This possibility of the others, of being able to be wounded, and the opposite actuality, of not being wounded, as well as the actuality of the heel's being wounded and its opposite possibility, of also not being wounded, the Greeks unite in the imagination through the myth, Achilles' immersion in the Lethe, according to which the unwounded parts could at the same time not be wounded and the wounded part alone could only be wounded.
zh: 阿喀琉斯死了，脚踵上中了一箭。
他同样可能在身上其余任何一处受伤。
所以那个部位上的伤是最大的偶然。
就箭的方向来说，它又是完全被规定了的。
但被射中的那一处，就其余部位来看（既然它和这些部位构成一个整体，就必然要被联系到它们），是被区分出来的受伤的、被射中的部位。
其余部位有受伤的可能，与之相反的是没受伤的现实性；脚踵有受伤的现实性，与之相反的又是也可能不受伤的可能——希腊人在想象力里用神话把这两面结合起来，那就是阿喀琉斯浸入忘川：按这个神话，没受伤的部位同样不可能受伤，而受伤的部位则只能受伤。

en: Before Lycurgus, after an absence of ten years, returned to Sparta in order now to carry out the completed plan of his legislation, he asked the oracle at Delphi about it.
The Pythia called him, in the name of Apollo, a friend and darling of the gods.
She told him that he was more a god than a man.

She declared to him that Apollo approved the plan he had made; if he could bring about the acceptance of his laws, there would be no better-ordered republic in the world than the Lacedaemonian. - After he had now gradually introduced his laws, he betook himself again to the oracle, which gave the pronouncement that he had sufficiently provided for making the Lacedaemonians as happy as virtuous, and that if they constantly kept his laws, they would enjoy eternal fame and happiness. - If the Lacedaemonians and the other Greeks had been capable of subjecting themselves to positive divine laws, indeed of having only a concept of them, should the Lacedaemonians [then] not have obliged the other Greeks, not have preached to them, to likewise adopt their constitution, which a pronouncement of the general oracle had declared the most perfect?
Would the others not, in order to be consistent, have had to adopt the same? - But the Greeks were a free nation, which did not let even a god give it laws.
This motive, confirmation by the deity, was foreign to them.
zh: 吕库古在外十年之后回到斯巴达，为的是现在就把自己那已经完成的立法计划付诸实行；在这之前，他为了这件事去问了德尔斐的神谕。
皮提亚以阿波罗的名义称他为诸神的朋友和宠儿。
她对他说，他与其说是人，不如说是神。

她向他说明，阿波罗赞同他所制定的计划；只要他能促成人们接受他的法律，世上就不会有比拉栖代孟人的共和国安排得更好的共和国了。——等他逐步把自己的法律推行开来之后，他又去了神谕那里，神谕宣称，他已经作出了足够的安排，使拉栖代孟人既幸福又有美德，而且只要他们始终遵守他的法律，他们就会享有永恒的名声和幸福。——假如拉栖代孟人和其余的希腊人能够服从实证的神圣法律，哪怕只是对这些法律有一个概念，那么拉栖代孟人[岂不是]就该去要求别的希腊人、就该向他们宣讲，要他们也照样接受自己的宪法吗？而这部宪法曾被普遍神谕的一句话宣布为最完善的。
其余的希腊人为了前后一致，不也本该接受同一部宪法吗？——但希腊人是一个自由的民族，它连神也不让来给它立法律。
这个理由，即由神性来确认，对他们来说是陌生的。

en: After the downfall of Roman and Greek freedom, when men had been deprived of the dominion of their ideas over the objects, the genius of humanity separated itself.

The spirit of the corrupt multitude said to the objects: I am yours, take me up!, threw itself into the stream of them, let itself be swept away by them and perished in their change. - The spirit of the Stoics did the opposite.

It said: you are foreign to my essence, which knows nothing of you; I rule you in my idea; you may be as you will, that is indifferent to me, you are too contemptible to me for me to want to lay hands on you. - Other spirits felt that the objects ought to be otherwise, but they did not have the courage to grasp them and to form them.
The superior power of the latter weighed upon them and left them only the feeling of their powerlessness.

One part of these spirits formed for itself objects invisible to the senses, which it found in the delusion of the people, but transferred its ideas onto them and implored them: take me up into your essence, appear to us, reveal yourselves to us, draw us to you, do you rule us!

They were called theurges. - Another part of the latter spirits heard of a similar new object, fled the outer objects that were denied to it, threw itself into the arms of the faith that that invisible thing would rule both itself and the outer objects, - and were called Christians.
The developed church has united both, the wish of the Stoics and that of those spirits broken within themselves.
It allows man to live in the whirl of the objects, and promises, through easy exercises, manipulations, lip-movements etc., at the same time to raise himself above them.
The wish of the theurges has really come only here and there into the head of so-called Christian enthusiasts.
This union has never really become a trade, as the rest has.
zh: 罗马和希腊的自由衰亡之后，当人对对象的观念统治被夺走时，人类的天才就分离了。
败坏了的人群的精神对对象说：我是你们的，收下我吧！它投身于对象的洪流，任凭自己被它们卷走，在它们的变换中沉没了。——斯多亚派的精神做的正好相反。
它说：你们对我的本质来说是陌生的，我的本质对你们一无所知；我在我的观念里统治你们；你们爱怎么样就怎么样，这对我无所谓，你们太可鄙，我不屑于动手去碰你们。——另一些精神感到，对象本应另是一样，但他们没有勇气去抓住它们、塑造它们。
对象的强大压在它们身上，只给它们留下自己无能为力的感受。
这些精神里的一部分，为自己造出了感官看不见的对象——它是在民众的妄想里碰上这些对象的——却把自己的观念转加到它们身上，向它们祈求：把我纳入你们的本质吧，向我们显现吧，把你们自己向我们启示出来吧，把我们吸引到你们那里去吧，让你们来统治我们吧！
他们被叫作神术师。——后一类精神中的另一部分听人说起一个类似的新对象，就逃离那些得不到的外在对象，投身于这样一种信仰的怀抱：那个看不见的东西会统治他们自己和那些外在对象——于是他们被叫作基督徒。
发展成形的教会把两者结合了起来：斯多亚派的愿望，和那些在自身中破裂的精神的愿望。
它允许人活在对象的旋涡里，并且许诺，人通过轻松的练习、手法、嘴唇的动作等等，同时还能超越它们。
神术师的愿望，其实只是零零星星地进过一些所谓基督教狂热者的脑子。
这种结合从来没有像其余那些东西那样，真正变成一门行当。

en: In the series of the revelations of God, or in the successive descent and generation of his shapes, the revelations of the same as sun, stars, sea, air, love preceded his revelation as man.
The latter shape was necessary in the graded sequence of his generations.
Nature was, through the arrangement of the Roman state, which took away freedom from almost the whole known earth, subjected to a law foreign to man, and the connection with it was torn apart.
Its life became stones and timbers; the gods became created and serving beings.
Where violence stirred, where beneficence revealed itself, where greatness ruled, there was man's heart and character.
Theseus became a hero to the Athenians only after his death.
To Demetrios and Antigonos they sacrificed only as to men who had passed away.
The Roman Caesars were deified.
Apollonius of Tyana did miracles.
The great was no longer supernatural but contrary to nature, for nature was no longer divine, hence no longer beautiful and no longer free.
In this separation of nature and the divine, a man became the connector of both, hence the reconciler and redeemer. - But the people of the Jews has gone down to hell in the wickedness of hatred.
What of it still tottered on upon the earth afterwards has remained as a sign.

As the more recent peoples must have all forms of humanity beneath them, the noble ones to be sure only in suffering, so too does this people still stand beneath them as the ideal of the most reprobate.
In Homer's world the manifoldness closes off downwards with Thersites, who has only a useless tongue.
Yet after he has been beaten, a tear falls from his eye.
Full of fear and silent he sits down and wipes the tear away.
His fear and his silence acknowledge more powerful human beings.
This receptivity, at least for the better, had to remain with the worst of Homer's human beings.

But in a more recent human world one sees, beside Amalie's heavenly pure soul, Schufterle's children roasting at the fire, and when the captain, now becoming conscious of his fate, threatens the robbers with a terrible muster, they think he is in a worse mood today.
In such a jumble of different races, which together are called by the systematizer man, the Jew has his place.
One man among the Jews has good-naturedly let God say: whoever does not heed my commandments, him will I punish unto the third and fourth generation.
But the Furies of their religion already whip them into their hundredth.

They do believe themselves, however, perhaps not punished when the Christian throws them down the stairs because they are Jews, when for the gain of a few kreutzers they have let themselves be basely treated for hours on end and also begin to chatter in the third hour, - and when they come back the next day.
zh: 在上帝的一系列启示中，或者说在他的诸形态先后相承的谱系与生成中，同一个上帝的作为太阳、星辰、海、空气、爱的那些启示，先行于他作为人的启示。
后一个形态在他生成的阶梯次序中是必然的。
自然由于罗马国家的制度而被置于一种对人陌生的法律之下，这种制度几乎夺去了整个已知大地的自由，而与自然的联系也被扯断了。
自然的生命变成了石头和木头；诸神变成了被造出来的、供役使的存在者。
哪里暴力在动，哪里善行显露出来，哪里伟大在主宰，那里就有人的心和品格。
对雅典人来说，忒修斯要到死后才成为英雄。
他们对德米特里和安提戈诺斯献祭，只是把他们当作已经逝去的人。
罗马的诸恺撒被神化了。
提亚纳的阿波罗尼奥斯行奇迹。
伟大的东西不再超乎自然，而是违背自然，因为自然不再是神圣的，所以也不再美，不再自由。
在自然与神圣者的这种分离中，一个人成了两者的联结者，所以也就是和解者和救赎者。 —— 但犹太人这个民族却在仇恨的邪恶中下到了地狱。
它此后还在地上摇摇晃晃走着的那些东西，留下来成了一个记号。
正如较新的诸民族必须把一切人性的形态都置于自己之下——高贵的形态当然只是在受苦中才置于自己之下——这个民族也仍然作为最被唾弃者的理想处在它们之下。
在荷马的世界里，杂多向下以忒尔西忒斯收尾，他只有一条没用的舌头。
但在他挨打之后，一滴泪从眼里落下。
他满心恐惧，一言不发地坐下，把眼泪擦掉。
他的恐惧和他的沉默承认了更有力的人。
这种至少对较好的东西的感受力，必定还留在荷马笔下最坏的人身上。
但在一个较新的人的世界里，人们在阿玛莉亚那圣洁纯净的灵魂旁边，看见舒夫特尔的孩子们在火上烤着，而当上尉现在开始意识到自己的命运、以可怕的检阅威胁那群强盗时，他们却以为他今天心情不好。
在这样一种各个族类混在一起的乱局中——它们合起来被系统化者称作人——犹太人占着自己的位置。
犹太人中有一个人好脾气地让上帝说：谁不看重我的诫命，我就要惩罚他，直到第三代和第四代。
但他们宗教的复仇女神已经在鞭打他们，一直打到他们的第一百代。
可是他们也许并不觉得自己受了惩罚：当基督徒因为他们是犹太人而把他们推下楼梯的时候，当他们为了几个十字币的赚头而让自己一连几个钟头被人下贱地对待、到了第三个钟头还开始闲聊的时候，——还有当他们第二天再来的时候。

en: What a cultivated taste and a prejudice-free reason, which know how to value the nobility of the Greek spirit in its whole extent, in all its modifications, still find to object to, is the ignoble element in the passion of love, which among the nations of German descent in more recent history has won a wholly different, more sublime shape.
Should this phenomenon not also be connected with the spirit of their free life?

If a knight from the times of chivalry recounted to an Aristides the deeds that he performed for his beloved, the adventures that he endured for her, the long series of years each moment of which was devoted with an iron patience to one single purpose that his beloved had set him, if such a one had left Aristides in doubt as to who the object of this activity had been; - or if a noble young man painted for this very Aristides, with all the fire of imagination and in just the same indeterminate manner, the beauty of his beloved object, described to him the deep respect that he felt for it, the holiness and purity of his feeling, the enthusiasm in its presence, how it was the single interest of his life to work and to breathe for it; - would Aristides, who did not know to whom all this expenditure of feelings, deeds, enthusiasm was devoted, would he not speak against it somewhat as follows: I dedicated my life to my fatherland; I knew nothing higher than its freedom and its welfare; I worked for it without any claim to distinction or power or wealth, but I am conscious that I did not do so much for it, did not feel such single and deep respect for it; I know otherwise of Greeks who did more, were more highly inspired, but I know none who attained to this height of feeling of self-denial on which you stand.
And what was the object of this high life of yours?
It must be infinitely greater, worthier than the highest that I could think, greater than fatherland and freedom!
zh: 一种有教养的品味和一种不带偏见的理性，懂得在希腊精神的全部范围、它的全部变式中估量其高贵，而它们仍然要挑剔的，是爱的激情中不高贵的东西，这种激情在德意志血统的诸民族那里，在较新的历史中获得了完全不同的、更崇高的形态。
这个现象难道不也和他们自由生活的精神相关联吗？

如果一个骑士出身的、来自骑士制度时代的骑士向一个阿里斯提德斯讲述他为自己的情人做下的事迹，他为她经受的冒险，那长长的一串年头，其中每一个瞬间都以铁一般的耐心献给他的情人交给他的唯一目的，如果这样一个人还让阿里斯提德斯弄不清这番作为的对象究竟是谁；——或者如果一个高贵的年轻人用想象力的全部火焰、同样不确定地向这位阿里斯提德斯描画他所爱对象的美丽，向他描述自己对他感到的深深敬重、自己情感的神圣和纯净、在他近旁的振奋，说为它工作、为它呼吸是自己生命唯一的关切；——阿里斯提德斯并不知道这全部的情感、事迹、振奋是献给谁的，他难道不会这样反驳说：我把我的生命献给了我的祖国；我不知道有比它的自由和它的福祉更高的东西；我为它工作，完全不要求什么显赫、权力或财富，但我意识到，我并没有为它做这么多，并没有感到如此专一而深沉的敬重；我也认识一些希腊人，他们做得更多，振奋得更高，但我不认识有谁达到你们所站的那种自我舍弃的感受的高度。
而你们这种崇高生活的对象又是什么呢？
它必定无限地比我所能想到的最高者更大、更可敬，比祖国和自由更大！

en: The unbridled imagination of the women of the Middle Ages has raged about in the horrors of witchcraft, in the craving to exercise petty envy and revenge on others, and has brought them to the stake.
To the Greek women, in the bacchic festivals, a permitted free scope was given to rage themselves out.
Upon the exhaustion of the body and of the imagination followed a calm stepping back into the circle of ordinary feeling and customary life.
The wild Maenad was the rest of the time a reasonable woman.

There witches, here maenads, there the object of the imagination devilish grimaces, here a beautiful, vine-leafed god; there with that associated satisfaction of envy, lust for revenge, hatred, here nothing but purposeless pleasure, often going as far as raging frenzy; there progress from single fits of madness to complete and lasting derangement of the spirit, here a stepping back into ordinary life; there the age regarded this disguised frenzy not as an illness, but as the most blasphemous outrage, which could be atoned for only with stakes, here this need of some female imaginations and temperaments was something holy, for whose outbursts festivals were given, [which were] sanctioned by the state and thereby brought into the possibility of becoming harmless.
zh: 中世纪妇女那种没有约束的想象力，在巫术的种种可怕勾当里，在要向别人发泄小小的嫉妒和报复的嗜好里横冲直撞，把她们送上了火刑堆。
希腊妇女则在酒神节里得到了一个被允许的活动空间，可以尽情发泄自己。
身体和想象力耗尽之后，接着便是安静地退回到寻常感受和旧日生活的圈子里。
其余的时候，狂野的迈那德是个有理智的女人。

那边是女巫，这边是迈那德；那边想象力的对象是魔鬼般的鬼脸，这边是一个美丽的、缠着葡萄藤的神；那边与之相伴的是嫉妒、复仇欲和仇恨的满足，这边却只是无目的的、常常闹到发狂地步的快乐；那边是从一次次疯癫发作走向精神的彻底而持久的错乱，这边是退回到寻常生活；那边这个时代并不把这种装出来的疯劲看成一种病，而看成最亵渎神明的恶行，只能用火刑堆来赎，这边这种需要——某些女性的想象力和气质的需要——却是神圣的东西，人们为它的爆发设了节庆，[这些节庆]得到国家的认可，因而才有了变得无害的可能。

en: The voice of the Catholic clergy is almost close to hoarseness.

Their own estate, the separating monastic dress, the being cut off from all human beings and relations, that which at every moment strains their muscles to inner reaction and holding back, does not let the voice come out of the breast, which in most of them is also sunken, but it screeches finely out of the throat, yet not purely.
Protestant preachers have the more solemn voice of common life.
When the Catholic voice strains itself to the loud speaking of preaching, it is so screeching through, whimpering, screaming.
zh: 天主教教士的声音几乎快要嘶哑了。
他们自己的等级、把人隔开的修士服、与所有人和所有关系割断的状态、每时每刻把他们的肌肉绷紧去做内心反应和自我克制的那回事，使声音不从胸腔里出来——在大多数人那里胸腔也已经塌陷了——而是从喉咙里细声尖叫，却不清亮。
新教牧师有着寻常生活那种更庄重的声音。
当天主教的声音使劲拔高到讲道的那种高声说话时，它就那样尖利刺耳、呜呜咽咽地叫喊。

en: Contempt of human beings.
Everyone is accustomed to judge others according to the rule that he has made for himself for humanity, and to demand that he be so.
Only long experience of the world or an excess of goodness of heart brings us back from this.
This demand is chiefly peculiar to the Europeans.
It is a kind of obstinacy.

Thus it is also a sign of our time and nothing further - not high culture, not an approach to the end of humanity, to perfection -, the public judging of characters, e.g. of a Rousseau, according to the rules of reason.

Besides that everyone should first reach into his own bosom, it is only virtue alone, which gives itself its rules, that can judge and demand, but no human being has against another the right to put himself in the place of virtue and, presenting himself as its person, to make demands on others.
Everyone can answer such a one: virtue has the right to demand this of me, but not you.
zh: 对人的蔑视。
每个人都习惯于按自己为人类定下的规则去评判别人，并要求别人就是这样。
只有长久的世事经验，或者心地的过分善良，才能把我们从这里拉回来。
这种要求尤其是欧洲人特有的。
这是一种固执。
所以，按理性的规则公开评判各种性格，比如评判一个卢梭，这也只是我们这个时代的一个标志，此外什么也不是——不是高度的文化，不是向人类的目的、向完善靠近。
除了每个人都该先摸一摸自己的胸膛之外，能评判和提要求的只有那自己给自己定规则的美德，但任何人都没有权利在别人面前把自己摆在美德的位置上，充当美德的化身，向别人提要求。
每个人都可以这样回答他：美德有权利向我要求这一点，但你没有。

en: In the states of modern times, security of property is the pivot on which the whole legislation turns, to which most rights of the citizens refer.
In many a free republic of antiquity, the strict right of property, the care of all our authorities, the pride of our states, has already been encroached upon by the constitution of the state.
In the Lacedaemonian constitution, security of property and of industry was a point that hardly came into consideration at all, that, one can almost say, was forgotten.
In Athens the rich citizens were usually robbed of a part of their fortune.
But one used an honourable pretext for the person one wished to rob: one transferred to him an office that demanded an enormous expenditure.
Whoever in the tribes, into which the citizens were divided, was elected to a costly office, could look about among the citizens of his tribe whether he might not find a richer one.
If he believed he had found such a one, and this one asserted that he was less rich, then the former could propose to him an exchange of their fortunes, which the latter was not allowed to refuse.

How dangerous the disproportionate wealth of some citizens is to even the freest form of constitution, and how capable it is of destroying freedom itself, history shows in the example of a Pericles at Athens, of the patricians in Rome, whose downfall the threatening influence of the Gracchi and others sought in vain to check through proposals of agrarian laws, of the Medici at Florence - and it would be an important investigation, how much of the strict right of property would have to be sacrificed to the lasting form of a republic.
One has perhaps done wrong to the system of sans-culottism in France, if one sought the source of the greater equality of property intended by it solely in the greed for plunder.
zh: 在近代的国家里，财产的安全是整个立法围着转的轴心，公民的大部分权利都与之相关。
在古代某些自由的共和国里，严格的财产权——我们一切官府的操心事，我们这些国家的骄傲——就已经被国家宪法损害了。
在拉栖第梦的宪法里，财产和产业的安全几乎根本不在考虑之列，几乎可以说，是被忘掉了的。
在雅典，富有的公民通常会被剥夺掉一部分财产。
不过人们会为想要剥夺的那个人找一个体面的借口：给他安一个职位，而这个职位需要巨大的开销。
在公民所分成的各个部族里，谁被选去担任一个花费很大的职务，谁就可以在自己的部族里四下看看，能不能找到一个更有钱的人。
如果他觉得自己找到了这样一个人，而这个人声称自己没有那么多钱，那么前者就可以向他提出交换两人的财产，后者不得拒绝。
一些公民的不成比例的财富，对哪怕最自由的宪法形式有多么危险，又多么能够摧毁自由本身，历史已经用雅典的伯里克利、罗马的贵族这些例子表明出来了——格拉古兄弟等人凭借土地法的提案，想用自己那咄咄逼人的影响力去阻止这些人的没落，却是徒劳——还有佛罗伦萨的美第奇；而为了共和国的持久形式，究竟要牺牲掉多少严格的财产权，那会是一项重要的研究。
人们也许冤枉了法国的无套裤汉主义制度，如果人们把它所意图的更大的财产平等的来源，单单到掠夺欲里去找。
